name: mention-input
purpose: A plain-text field that suggests people, tags, or other entities when the user types a trigger character such as @ or #. Suggestions come from an async provider (debounced, aborted when superseded); inserted mentions are kept as structured tokens { id, label, trigger, start, end } whose offsets follow every edit. Nothing is rendered as HTML. A Form control with a hidden input carrying the JSON value.
whenToUse: Comments, notes, and messages that reference people (@) or topics (#) by id.
Any text where the server needs to know exactly which entity was referenced, not just the typed name.
whenNotToUse: Picking one or more entities without free text: use Combobox or Multi Select.
Formatted text with bold, lists, or links: use Rich Text Editor.
Values that must not contain free text.
responsive: The field fills its container; the suggestion popup is at most 24rem wide and the viewport width, and flips above the field when there is no room below.
rtl: The text follows the document direction; the popup aligns to the field's inline start.
theme: Global tokens only: field surface, selected and hover colors for suggestions, focus ring. Forced colors use Highlight and HighlightText for the active suggestion.
security: Text, labels, and suggestions are rendered with textContent; the value is plain text with offsets, never HTML. Provider results are validated (id and label strings) before rendering.
dataHandling: The provider is called with the query only; no persistence or telemetry. Queries are aborted through AbortSignal when superseded.

performance.testedScale: Texts of 10,000 characters with 200 mentions; up to 50 suggestions shown (maxSuggestions).

limitations: Mentions are not highlighted inside the field (a native textarea cannot style ranges); they are plain text with tokens in the value.
Inserting a suggestion replaces the field value programmatically, so the browser's undo history does not include it.
Queries stop at whitespace: multi-word labels are found by their first word.
unsupported: Rich text, HTML, or Markdown rendering.
antiPatterns: Parsing @names out of the text on the server instead of using the mention ids.
Providers that ignore the AbortSignal and do expensive work for stale queries.
